title: Tenant queue fairness and adaptive admission playbook for hosted GPU exhaustion
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: During a hosted API capacity incident on 2026-03-09 we observed sustained GPU pool exhaustion caused by a small set of tenants issuing long-context, high-concurrency streaming requests. The event produced a self-reinforcing queue buildup where backend admission retries and prefetch attempts amplified latency and prevented autoscaler priming. This ticket captures the postmortem follow-ups: a prioritized playbook for adaptive admission, tenant fairness windows, improved cache eviction heuristics, and telemetry required to prevent recurrence.

Goal: Deliver an operational playbook and code changes that (1) bound per-tenant admission pressure, (2) reduce queue amplification from failed prefetches/evictions, (3) provide fast automated mitigations during pool saturation, and (4) surface clear SLO-grade telemetry for oncall to act with confidence.
timeline: 2026-03-09T01:12Z - First signs: hostpool latency spikes, initial alarms on per-GPU token latency
2026-03-09T01:20Z - Queue depth climbs; aggressive prefetch/retry logic kicks in for a subset of tenants
2026-03-09T01:35Z - Autoscaler fails to prime due to short-lived bursts; eviction thrash observed
2026-03-09T02:05Z - Mitigation: routing team applied temporary per-tenant soft caps and diverted non-critical traffic
2026-03-09T03:10Z - Pools begin to drain after manual tenant throttles and spot-prewarm actions
root_cause: A combination of factors: (1) tenant workloads with high-concurrency long-context streams produced disproportionate KV cache pressure and GPU memory churn; (2) prefetch and retry logic lacked backoff coordination with admission scoring which produced repeated queue amplification; (3) autoscaler hysteresis/priming thresholds were tuned for bandwidth rather than abrupt tail-heavy bursts, delaying capacity addition; (4) insufficient per-tenant admission visibility in metrics made early detection slow.
action_items: Liam Ross - Implement per-tenant rolling admission budget (token-based window) in the edge admission proxy to cap instantaneous concurrent requests and enforce fair share. Due: 2026-03-28
Sofia Nguyen - Add prefix-aware KV-cache eviction policy: prefer evicting large cold KV segments from tenants exceeding their rolling budget. Prototype and bench: 2026-03-22
Diego Morales - Replace aggressive prefetch retrier with coordinated backoff that consults admission proxy state to avoid amplification. Unit tests and integration: 2026-03-25

Asha Patel - Tune autoscaler priming heuristics: add a burst-aware fast-path to prewarm pools when queue slope > threshold and probability of sustained burst is high. Experiment and rollout: target 2026-04-02
Maya Chen - Instrument per-tenant admission metrics (rolling token usage, queue-share, failed-prefetch-rate) and add dashboard + alert runbook. Dashboard live: 2026-03-20
Platform SRE - Publish a one-page capacity playbook for oncall: steps to apply quick tenant soft caps, routing fallback, and safe drain procedures. Draft: 2026-03-18
Runtime team - Implement a soft-eviction path that preserves critical KV prefixes tied to in-flight requests to reduce retry-driven recomputation. Spike and benchmark: 2026-03-30
Security/Compliance - Review changes for telemetry and tenant caps to ensure no leakage between tenants. Review complete: 2026-03-27
followups: Run a red-team simulation with synthetic heavy-tail tenants to validate admission budgets and autoscaler fast-path (owner: Platform SRE). Target: 2026-04-09

After implementation, measure 99th percentile tail latency reduction and cost delta for two representative workloads; produce a short analysis doc for product and sales (owner: Performance Analytics). Due: 2026-04-15
Coordinate with Solutions and Account teams to notify customers who were impacted and offer mitigation guidance for tenant-side rate shaping (owner: Customer Success). Ongoing
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant rolling admission budget is enforced end-to-end and can be adjusted via console flags
New KV eviction policy demonstrably reduces recompute/failed-prefetch rate in benchmarks by >=40% for tail workloads
Autoscaler primes within target window for synthetic bursts that match historical worst-case slopes
Dashboards and alerts surface per-tenant pressure with sub-1min resolution and oncall runbook steps validated in a playbook run
